note.after_visit_summary: You came in because you've been feeling fluttering or skipped beats in your chest for about 3 weeks, mostly at night. These episodes last just a few seconds and happen several times a day. You haven't had chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting. We checked your heart rhythm with an ECG, which was normal. Your symptoms are likely due to extra heartbeats that are common and usually harmless, especially when triggered by caffeine, energy drinks, and lack of sleep. You're currently drinking about 4 cold brews and 2 energy drinks each day and sleeping around 5 hours. To help, we recommend gradually cutting back caffeine over the next two weeks to no more than one regular coffee per day and stopping energy drinks completely. Aim for at least 7 hours of sleep each night. We're also checking a thyroid test, blood count, and electrolytes to rule out other causes. If the fluttering continues after six weeks of these changes, we may use a monitor to record your heart rhythm for two weeks. Seek emergency care if you faint, develop chest pain with the fluttering, or have a racing heartbeat that doesn't stop. Otherwise, return for follow-up in six weeks. Continue taking your birth control pill daily and melatonin 3 mg at night as needed for sleep. You have no known drug allergies.
